corrections.text: The article says, citing The Hacker News and SafeDep, that both releases carry "the same few-line loader". Socket's analysis says the two loaders do the same thing but are not identical code: the bee-js loader requests /v1/analytics with a 3-second timeout and swallows request errors, while the Swarm Desktop loader requests /v1/electron with no timeout or error handling; both pass the server's reply to new Function and send the same X-Ethersphere header.

The article says, citing The Hacker News, that both releases "came from bee-worker", Ethersphere's release-automation account. Socket reports that two GitHub accounts were compromised, and that the commit repairing the Swarm Desktop build workflow used for 0.56.2 was pushed through a maintainer's account rather than bee-worker.

The article says "The Swarm Desktop maintainers wrote" that 0.56.2 "was published by an attacker using stolen CI credentials and has been withdrawn". The quoted words are the commit message of pull request #582, written by a single maintainer (The Hacker News: "one of them wrote"); the pull request description words the finding differently ("built and published by an attacker using stolen CI credentials").
